newsitem.title: UK: UK consumer lead indicator at record high in Sept.
newsitem.headline: UK consumer lead indicator at record high in Sept.

text.p: The NTC consumer industries' leading indicator rose in September and hit a new record high for the fourth month in a row.

NTC said upward pressures came from tighter labour market conditions, likely to translate into rising wages and real incomes over the next year and low interest rates and improved consumer confidence.
NTC added that significant growth in output of consumer goods and an increasingly buoyant television advertising market also contributed upward pressure on the leading indicator.
The indicator has historically been a useful guide to the business cycle, tending to move ahead of it by one year.
"The sharp rise in the indicator since the beginning of the year therefore signals a considerable increase in the forces of economic expansion next year," NTC said.
It said it suggested a sharp pick up in the rate of GDP growth driven by higher consumer spending.
NTC is an independent research group. It also compiles the data for the UK purchasing managers' index.
